title: A finite union of sets D(f) ∩ V(g_1,…,g_n) in an affine spectrum is a finite disjoint union of such sets
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Call a subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ *basic* if it is of the form $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\dots,g_n)$ with $f,g_1,\dots,g_n\in A$, $n\ge0$, where $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $V(g_1,\dots,g_n)=\{\mathfrak p:g_1,\dots,g_n\in\mathfrak p\}$. If $B_1,\dots,B_m\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ ($m\ge0$) are basic, then there are finitely many basic subsets $C_1,\dots,C_p\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ ($p\ge0$), pairwise disjoint, with $B_1\cup\dots\cup B_m=C_1\cup\dots\cup C_p$.

source.place: no single place: the refinement step 'After refining the partition further' of Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex line 12049), for the basic sets of Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P (algebra.tex line 5434); compare Topology, Lemma Tag 09Y4 (topology.tex line 5607), which refines a finite family of constructible sets into a disjoint stratification by constructible sets but does not keep the pieces basic

proof.text: The empty family has the empty disjoint refinement. For a nonempty family, construct refinements inductively. Suppose a finite pairwise-disjoint family \(\mathcal C_t\) of basic sets has union \(B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_t\). For every \(C\in\mathcal C_t\), apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-basic-set-difference] to write \(C\setminus B_{t+1}\) as a finite pairwise-disjoint family of basic sets. These families remain pairwise disjoint for distinct \(C\), since the \(C\)'s are disjoint.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0, proof at line 12049 (the refinement is asserted there); induction and set operations written out by the agent

proof.text: It remains to add the part of \(B_{t+1}\) not already covered. Start with the one-element family \(\{B_{t+1}\}\). Process the finitely many members \(C\) of \(\mathcal C_t\) one at a time: replace every current basic piece \(P\) by the finite pairwise-disjoint basic decomposition of \(P\setminus C\) supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-basic-set-difference]. At each replacement the pieces stay pairwise disjoint, and after all \(C\)'s the resulting finite family \(\mathcal R\) consists of pairwise-disjoint basic sets with \(\bigcup\mathcal R=B_{t+1}\setminus\bigcup\mathcal C_t\). The family formed by all pieces of the \(C\setminus B_{t+1}\) differences together with \(\mathcal R\) is finite and pairwise disjoint, and its union is \(\bigcup\mathcal C_t\cup B_{t+1}\). Thus it is \(\mathcal C_{t+1}\). Induction through \(t=m\) gives the required finite pairwise-disjoint basic family; when \(m=0\), take the empty family.
